detail: Between 5% and 10% below the high counts as a pullback, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,237.17 on Monday, about 7.4% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October, after a 4.7% jump took it out of correction territory. Big swings both ways are common after sharp falls, so one strong day doesn't mean the worry is over.
source: CNBC and AP closing figures, 23 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was broad on Monday: on the Nasdaq 2,804 shares rose and 746 fell, nearly four risers for every faller. A rally that lifts most shares, not just a few giants, is a healthier sign than one carried by a handful of names.
source: Reuters closing breadth via Investing.com, 23 Nov

detail: Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield ended Monday little changed at 4.92% as investors weighed the share rebound against bets on Fed rate rises. Safe bonds paying close to 5% still set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: Hammerstone and Armstrong Economics closing levels, 23 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 96% on Monday, and traders saw about an 85% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: CME FedWatch via Hammerstone, 23 Nov; LSEG data via Reuters, 23 Nov

detail: Between $65 and $90 a barrel counts as normal, and Brent crude fell 3.5% to settle at $89.37 on Monday, just under the line and its lowest since late August, as a Libyan pipeline restarted and Middle East supply rose. Cheaper oil eases pressure on inflation, though prices are still high by recent standards.
source: ICE settlement via Dow Jones and Reuters, 23 Nov
